title: Performance timing
lede: Wall-clock and monotonic timing grouped together, the way real JS/Node group them. Date follows the host's time zone as Node's does (local getters, the component constructor, toString), with Invalid Date for an unparseable string; the remaining divergence is the plain-number Date representation, so a setter needs a named variable and a zone outside the built-in name table prints its abbreviation in toString. performance and perf_hooks are Node's own user-timing code ported to TypeScript: marks and measures are entries on a timeline, observers receive them on a later turn of the loop, and histograms time the event loop.

entries.name: performance.now()
entries.description: Milliseconds since the program's time origin (process start), as a double. The origin is captured once at process start, matching the spec's origin-relative reading; the clock is monotonic and nanosecond-grained, like libuv's uv_hrtime. Unlike Date.now(), it is not tied to wall-clock time.

returns.desc: Milliseconds since process start, as a double.

entries.name: performance.mark / measure / getEntries* / clearMarks / clearMeasures / timerify / timeOrigin
entries.statusRow: performance.mark / measure / getEntries* / clearMarks / clearMeasures / timerify / timeOrigin
entries.signature: performance.mark(name: string, options?: PerformanceMarkOptions): PerformanceMark; performance.measure(name: string, startMark?: string, endMark?: string): PerformanceMeasure; performance.measure(name: string, options: PerformanceMeasureOptions): PerformanceMeasure
entries.description: User timing as Node keeps it. mark(name) records a PerformanceMark (with an optional structured-cloned detail and startTime); measure(name, start?, end?) or measure(name, options) records a PerformanceMeasure spanning two marks or timestamps, through now when the end is omitted. getEntries/getEntriesByName/getEntriesByType read the timeline in start order; a mark that was never set throws a SyntaxError DOMException.
entries.snippet:
performance.mark("loop-start")
for (let i = 0; i < 200000; i++) { arr2.push(i) }
performance.mark("loop-end")
const loopMs: number = performance.measure("loop", "loop-start", "loop-end").duration

entries.name: Date
entries.signature: new Date(); new Date(ms); new Date(isoString); new Date(year, month, day?, hours?, minutes?, seconds?, ms?)
entries.description: A thin wrapper over milliseconds-since-epoch. Constructs from no argument (now), a millisecond number, an ISO string, or year/month/day/... fields (month 0-indexed, omitted trailing fields defaulting like real JS). Provides the local getFullYear/Month/Date/Day/Hours/Minutes/Seconds/Milliseconds and their getUTC* forms, getTimezoneOffset, getTime/valueOf, toISOString and toString, in the host's time zone as Node's are. An unparseable string makes an Invalid Date (getTime() is NaN).

returns.desc: A Date value (a plain number under the hood).

differences: toString's zone name comes from a built-in table of the common zones' abbreviations; a zone outside it prints the C library's abbreviation (GMT-0300 (-03) where Node says (Brasilia Standard Time))

entries.name: Date.now()
entries.description: Milliseconds since the epoch, via clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, ...). Wall-clock time, unlike performance.now().
entries.snippet:
const nowMs: number = Date.now()
const now: Date = new Date()

entries.name: Date.parse(string)
entries.description: Parses the ECMAScript date-time format (a date-only form as UTC, a date-time without an offset as local time, Z or a +HH:MM/-HH:MM offset) and V8's legacy forms: toString and toUTCString output, "Jul 15 2024", "2024/07/15 10:30".

returns.desc: Milliseconds since epoch, or NaN if unparseable.

entries.name: Date setters (setFullYear, setMonth, setDate, setHours, setMinutes, setSeconds, setMilliseconds, setTime)
entries.statusRow: Date setters (setFullYear, setMonth, setDate, setHours, setMinutes, setSeconds, setMilliseconds, setTime)
entries.description: Mutate a named Date variable in place and return the new timestamp, matching real JS.
differences: Requires a named-variable receiver (not a field access or call result — this compiler's Date is a plain number, not a reference object, so there's no heap location to mutate otherwise)
Only the single-argument form of each setter (no `setFullYear(y, m, d)`-style overloads)

entries.name: Date arithmetic (date ± durationMs, date - date, date += durationMs)
entries.statusRow: Date arithmetic (date ± durationMs, date - date, date += durationMs)
entries.signature: date + durationMs; date - durationMs; date - date; date += durationMs
entries.description: TypeScript rejects arithmetic on a Date, and so does the default strict lane: the millisecond count is getTime(). Under -compat=js, date + x concatenates the date string and date - x reads its millisecond count, matching real JS.

returns.desc: A string for +; a number for -, *, / and %.

differences: Under -compat=js, a compound `date += n` / `date -= n` keeps the variable a Date; JavaScript turns it into a string / a number (the plain `+`/`-` follow JavaScript)

entries.name: Date.prototype.toDateString()
entries.description: A fixed "Www Mon DD YYYY" shape (e.g. "Thu Jan 01 1970") in local time, as real JS gives it.

returns.desc: The date as a "Www Mon DD YYYY" string.

entries.snippet:
const launch: Date = new Date(1700000000000)
console.log(launch.toDateString())          // Tue Nov 14 2023

entries.name: Date.prototype.toLocaleDateString()
entries.description: Mimics real JS's default (en-US, no explicit locale) "M/D/YYYY" output.
entries.snippet:
const launch: Date = new Date(1700000000000)
console.log(launch.toLocaleDateString())    // 11/14/2023
differences: One fixed `"M/D/YYYY"` format (the default en-US shape) in local time; no locale argument or full `Intl`-style locale support

entries.name: PerformanceObserver
entries.description: Observes performance entries. observe({ entryTypes }) or observe({ type, buffered }) subscribes; the callback receives a PerformanceObserverEntryList (sorted by start time) on a later turn of the event loop, as in Node. disconnect() and takeRecords() work, and supportedEntryTypes lists the known types.

entries.name: createHistogram / monitorEventLoopDelay
entries.signature: createHistogram(options?: CreateHistogramOptions): RecordableHistogram; monitorEventLoopDelay(options?: EventLoopMonitorOptions): IntervalHistogram
entries.description: perf_hooks histograms: a RecordableHistogram takes record(value)/recordDelta()/add(other); monitorEventLoopDelay samples how late an interval timer runs while enabled. Both report count, min, max, mean, stddev, exceeds and percentiles, with BigInt forms.
entries.snippet:
import { createHistogram } from 'perf_hooks'
const h = createHistogram()
h.record(5); h.record(10); h.record(15)
console.log(h.count, h.min, h.max, h.percentile(50))   // 3 5 15 10
differences: A histogram keeps exact samples, not Node's HDR histogram (3 significant figures): a percentile of large values can differ in its last digits
